body:
_Migrated from issue #1184, filed 2026-07-28._

Observed on the e2e run for #1180 (run 30274438071): `hidden-books.spec.ts:237`
("Guest never receives a Hide action even when the instance feature is enabled")
failed on the first attempt and passed on retry.

```
Error: apiResponse.json: Response has been disposed

  241 |   await page.route('**/api/v1/auth/me', async (route) => {
  242 |     const response = await route.fetch();
> 243 |     const me = await response.json();
      |                               ^
  244 |     me.role = { ...(me.role ?? {}), anonymous: true, delete_books: false };
  246 |     await route.fulfill({ response, json: me });
```

The handler fetches the upstream response, awaits `.json()`, then fulfils. If the
page navigates (or the context tears down) while `.json()` is in flight, Playwright
disposes the response and the await rejects.

This is not one spec's problem. The same fetch-then-json-then-fulfil shape is used
at nine call sites:

- `book-detail.spec.ts:166, 213, 229, 277` — including the new long-metadata test added in #1178
- `entity-page-title.spec.ts:13`
- `help-banner-kofi.spec.ts:288`
- `hidden-books.spec.ts:194, 246`
- `sp2-display-options.spec.ts:47`

Any of them can flake the same way under the right timing.

Worth doing together with #1182 (the other known flake), because #1183 — promoting
the gate to required — should only happen once the gate is reliably green, and two
known-flaky patterns are exactly what would make a required gate untrustworthy again.

Likely fix is to guard the handler (fall back to `route.continue()` when the
response is already disposed) rather than to retry harder. Whatever shape it takes,
it should be applied to the pattern, not to the one spec that happened to flake.
title: hidden-books.spec.ts:237 flakes on 'Response has been disposed' (shared route.fulfill pattern)
